chunks: As for Masjid al-Sahlah, al-Sadiq عليه السلام said:

"If my uncle Zayd had sought refuge in it, Allah would have granted him refuge for a year. That is the site of the house of Idris عليه السلام, in which he used to sew, and it is the place from which Ibrahim عليه السلام went forth to the Amalekites. It is the place from which Dawud went forth to Jalut, and beneath it is a green rock in which is the image of the face of every Prophet whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created; and from beneath it the clay of every Prophet was taken; and it is the place of the Rider."
So it was said to him: "And who is the Rider?"
He said: "Al-Khiḍr عليه السلام. And as for Masjid Baratha in Baghdad, Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام prayed in it when he returned from fighting the people of al-Nahrawan."

key_terms.إِدْرِيسَ: Prophet Idris عليه السلام, whose house is said to have been at this site.
key_terms.الرَّاكِبُ: The Rider, identified in the narration as al-Khiḍr عليه السلام.
key_terms.الْعَمَالِقَةِ: The Amalekites, the people to whom Ibrahim عليه السلام is said here to have gone forth.
key_terms.صَخْرَةٌ خَضْرَاءُ: A green rock beneath the mosque described as bearing prophetic significance.
key_terms.طِينَةُ: Clay or primordial substance from which every Prophet's clay was taken.
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ السَّهْلَةِ: Masjid al-Sahlah, a mosque described here as possessing special sanctity and prophetic associations.

ai.seo_question: What virtues and sacred history are mentioned for Masjid al-Sahlah and Masjid Baratha in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the special merit and sacred history of Masjid al-Sahlah, linking it to several Prophets عليهم السلام and to al-Khiḍr عليه السلام. It also notes the significance of Masjid Baratha, where Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام prayed after the battle of al-Nahrawan.
